biological_reference.closest_mechanism: Dopaminergic reward-prediction-error teaching of a dorsal-striatal actor with a ventral-striatal value baseline (Schultz/Dayan/Montague 1997; O'Doherty 2004), with the demonstration arm's closest analog being observational/imitative acquisition of an action policy routed through lateral prefrontal rule representation.
dependencies: a parameterised actor whose parameters the teaching signal actually reaches (striatal actor, not a bounded prefrontal bias on a fixed value landscape)
a value baseline against which return is differenced (present here only as an EMA scalar, reinforce_baseline, EMA_DECAY 0.9)
an action-adequate representation for the actor to ride (V3-EXQ-737 found the frozen prediction latent action-INADEQUATE: 0.217 res/ep vs raw-obs 0.567 vs floor 1.0)
enough experience for the credit assignment to converge (90 episodes here)
biological_reference.divergence: Not a formal-definition import -- REINFORCE with an EMA baseline is a legitimate, biologically-motivated policy-gradient family. The divergence is one of LOCUS, not of formalism: the teaching signal is applied to two MODULATORY bias channels bounded at |0.1| and |2.0| rather than to an actor. Biologically the nearest thing to that arrangement is a prefrontal bias term added to an already-learned striatal action value -- which in real brains is a MODULATOR of a learned policy, never the sole substrate of policy learning. So the FAIL-shaped result here matches what would happen biologically if you ablated the striatal actor and tried to teach navigation through prefrontal bias alone: a discovered prerequisite, not a falsification of reward-density's relevance.

Minimum work, all `complicated (buildable)`. ABSORPTION (training side): (1) return per-phase mean/sd/min/max of `ep_reward` and of the REINFORCE advantage `ep_return - reinforce_baseline`, so a shaped-vs-sparse arm pair can be shown to have received different returns; (2) return the FRACTION of sampled outcome-buffer terms that survived `abs(adv) < ADV_MIN_THRESHOLD` (0.005) -- a run in which that fraction is ~0 received no gradient at all, whatever the reward was; (4) return the lateral-PFC bias-head last-linear weight-norm DELTA as a float, not only the existing boolean `moved > 1e-9` that V3-EXQ-1039's C0d gate used and that passed while the head's output stayed at chance; and return `hidden_dead_relu_frac` (already tracked as `_last_hidden_dead_relu_frac`, lateral_pfc_analog.py:284/:462-467, exposed in get_state() :555, needs `capture_head_diagnostics`) plus the per-tick candidate-summary PAIRWISE SPREAD, which together separate the three exactly-zero-gradient routes -- identical hidden rows, dead ReLU, hard-clamp saturation -- that are currently indistinguishable. Note for (4): `candidate_summary_degenerate` must be COMPUTED, not read. It is assigned only under `if self.config.rule_readout_consumer and k >= 2:` (lateral_pfc_analog.py:429-450) and `rule_readout_consumer` defaults False (:181; config.py:4207) and is not set by the all-ON recipe, so today the driver reads an `__init__` constant and C0d's degeneracy half is vacuous -- either enable the consumer, or record the pre/post-centering spread directly. CONVERSION (selection side) -- (3), REVISED: this is largely DRIVER-side recording of diagnostics E3 ALREADY EXPOSES in `e3.last_score_diagnostics`, not a build in this library: `e3_raw_score_range_mean`, `score_bias_range_mean`, `score_bias_to_raw_range_ratio`, `modulatory_authority_active/_scale_factor/_ratio_competitive/_normalize_basis`, plus the per-candidate count of distinct first-action classes. The quantity to record is the lPFC head's SHARE of the summed modulatory accum, NOT the absolute bias bound: with `use_modulatory_selection_authority` and `normalize_basis 'std'` E3 rescales the accum into competition with the raw spread (measured on this config: ratio 0.096-0.432), so `lateral_pfc_bias_scale = 0.1` is not the limiting quantity -- saturation of the hard clamp is the mechanism by which it can still bite. Companion driver-side convention (belongs in /queue-experiment, not in this entry): any experiment whose MANIPULATION is on the reward or training-signal channel must carry BOTH an absorption AND a conversion-capability readiness precondition -- see the routing note's five-item 1039a list. Absorption alone is NOT sufficient: a stationary policy still accrues a non-zero shaped return (`_dist_prev` is not reset on waypoint respawn, so ~1.5 bonus/ep accrues without moving), so 'arm returns differ' can go green on a policy that never moved.

Note carefully what is NOT claimed: the parameters DID change in both arms on seeds 43 and 44 (`lpfc_bias_head_moved: true`), so this is not an absence of parameter change -- learning item 9 gives a route by which changed parameters leave behaviour unchanged. The declared null was met for a reason that has nothing to do with reward density, and would have been met under any reward function whatsoever. (`lpfc_candidate_summary_degenerate` is deliberately NOT listed among the identical channels: it is a never-computed constant in this config -- see learning item 10.)

`demo_ce_final_loss` = 3.465736 on seed 42 is ln(32) to seven decimals, with num_candidates = 32 (ree_core/utils/config.py). A cross-entropy pinned at chance after 232 applied optimizer steps means the bias head's output stayed uniform across candidates -- and on that same seed `lpfc_bias_head_moved` reads False, i.e. 232 backward+optimizer-step calls moved the last-linear weight norm by less than 1e-9, which is the arithmetic signature of an exactly-zero gradient rather than a small one. Seeds 43 and 44 (14 and 22 applied steps) sit within 1e-3 of ln(32).

THE GATE BUILT FOR THIS DEFECT PASSED WHILE THE DEFECT WAS PRESENT, and that is the transferable lesson. The driver's Step 4.5 cross-model red-team raised F3 -- 'nothing certifies the ONE component every arm's training signal actually trains ever receives a non-zero gradient' -- and named the `demo_ce_final_loss == ln(K)` signature explicitly. The fix added readiness gate C0d, which tests `|weight-norm delta| > 1e-9` and a candidate-summary degeneracy flag. When a red-team names a failure signature, the gate should assert on THAT SIGNATURE (here: CE loss materially below ln(K)), not on a correlate of it.

A load-bearing criterion's non-degeneracy flag must be able to see the failure mode that would make the criterion vacuous. A TRAINING-SIDE ABSORPTION GATE IS NOT SUFFICIENT, because the eval side has its own way of being insensitive (red-team F1, confirmer reproduced by this session). The candidate pool E3 chooses from can collapse: at init, K=32, seed 42 carries 4 distinct first-action classes on 49 of 58 E3 ticks (5 on the rest) and SEED 43 CARRIES EXACTLY 2 ON 25 OF 25 TICKS. Two classes out of 32 candidates is a pool in which no bias on any candidate can produce more than a binary choice. This is a REGISTERED substrate condition, not a novelty: `mech294_coherence_magnitude_strengthening` (GFLAG-0183, 2026-09-09) records the ARC-065 SP-CEM pool as 'floor_clamped_at_2_distinct_first_action_classes ... vs the 4.5 distinct first-action classes MECH-341's falsifier treats as a diverse pool', and SD-061 (`implemented_pending_validation`) is the existing lever -- a difficulty-gated proposal-entropy regulator whose readout is `candidate_first_action_entropy`. A repair whose gate reproduces the defect it was written against is not a repair.

TWO -- in fact three -- distinct routes produce the identical exactly-zero-gradient signature, and naming only one was an unstated premise (red-team F5). For the last linear, dW_k = (p_k - y_k) h_k: this is exactly zero if (a) the hidden activations are IDENTICAL across candidates, since sum_k (p_k - y_k) = 0 makes the weighted sum and the bias gradient both vanish, or (b) the hidden ReLU is FULLY DEAD (h = 0 for all K). `LateralPFCAnalog` already tracks `_last_hidden_dead_relu_frac` (lateral_pfc_analog.py:284, populated :462-467, exposed in get_state() :555 as `hidden_dead_relu_frac`) and it is simply not recorded by the driver. The probe measures candidate-summary pairwise max distance at 0.0297-0.0517 (seed 42) and 0.0277-0.0462 (seed 43) AT INIT -- non-degenerate -- so any row-identity during the scored run is P0-INDUCED (`E2_TRAIN_IN_P1 = False`, allon_training.py:101, so E2 trains in P0 only). That is precisely ARC-065/MECH-314's registered finding: 'E2 world-forward compresses K diverse first-action candidates to identical first-step z_world (verified empirically 2026-05-25: cand_world_pairwise_dist=0.0000 across K=32 with 2-3 unique argmax action classes)' -- an independent corroboration of the 2-3-class figure from a different measurement five months earlier. Route (c), found while re-running F3's confirmer: because `rule_readout_consumer` is False, compute_bias takes the HARD-CLAMP branch (lateral_pfc_analog.py:483-485), and the substrate's own comment at :174-179 states that 'a saturated hard clamp has zero gradient, so REINFORCE cannot move the head', citing V3-EXQ-822's prop_delta of exactly 0.0. Route (c) cannot explain seed 42's first step (zero-init last linear means bias_raw starts at 0, unsaturated) but is live once the head moves. Distinguishing the three is one recording change, not three experiments.
